headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network defaults make CrewAI↔Cursor prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading tool misuse plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and uses shared memory among subagents; Cursor shares state via the local filesystem and can ingest clipboard/open files. That creates a plausible default bridge where one agent’s output can be treated as trusted input by the other, though not as directly as a raw MCP bridge.
conditions: IF CrewAI writes attacker-controlled text into a file that Cursor opens
IF Cursor copies agent output into clipboard or workspace content that CrewAI later reads
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents
Require human review before one agent reads the other’s files
Restrict CrewAI outputs to structured JSON
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI touches developer-passed crew data and has broad network egress; Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents, and also sends data to model providers/MCP servers. In a shared local-filesystem workflow, sensitive files can flow from Cursor into CrewAI or vice versa and then out to third-party APIs without a strong default barrier.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace containing secrets
IF Cursor or CrewAI forwards file contents to external model providers
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use separate OS users or containers
Disable network egress for one agent during sensitive tasks
Redact files before opening them in Cursor
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, execute shells, and spawn subprocesses; Cursor also modifies git state while CrewAI can operate in a shared-memory crew. On a shared directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide, and no locking is indicated in either profile.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or working directory
IF Cursor runs Yolo mode while CrewAI is also editing files
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git worktrees for parallel work
Turn off Yolo mode during shared edits
requires-engineering: add file-locking orchestration

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI’s role-playing crew can emit synthesized outputs that Cursor may then use in its agent loop and tool calls. Because Cursor can act on code and shell commands, a mistaken CrewAI output can cascade into concrete actions unless explicitly verified; the reverse path is also plausible through shared files.
conditions: IF Cursor consumes CrewAI-generated plans or facts without verification
IF CrewAI consumes Cursor-generated code suggestions as authoritative
mitigations: Require source citations before execution
Insert a human approval step between agents
Have Cursor validate CrewAI outputs against files
Limit CrewAI to drafting only
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor is closed-source and handles clipboard/open files with broad model-provider and MCP egress, while CrewAI is open-source but still processes developer-passed crew data. If regulated data is placed in the shared workspace, differing retention/logging and residency assumptions can create a compliance mismatch; the profiles do not prove a specific jurisdictional violation, so medium is the higher justified level.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace
IF Cursor’s provider or MCP logging retains that data longer than the operator expects
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Review provider retention settings
Disable clipboard use for sensitive material
Use a local-only workspace for regulated tasks
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
